text:
Nina Patel: Quick pass on the metrics visualization — specifically legend affordances, axis unit strategy, smoothing presets, and how we expose single extreme spikes on small screens. Short thread.
Omar Haddad: Thumbs up. Main pain: when charts are stacked vertically the y-axis units don't align, which makes cross-chart comparison hard. Can we offer a "sync axis units" option per dashboard?
Giselle Romero: +1 on sync axes. Also want a toggle to show Absolute vs Per-User normalized units (e.g., traces vs traces/user). Need copy to explain normalization.
Tom Becker: Legend UX: for mobile the current overflow menu is tricky. Proposal: slide-out legend panel on narrow widths with search and multi-select, and a compact inline legend for desktops that wraps into two rows.
Nina Patel: Good. For axis units I propose: default = compact SI (k, M) with a hover tooltip that displays the full value and unit; add a small per-chart badge: "Units: compact | full | per-user".
Omar Haddad: Outlier handling: instead of silently clipping, show a small capped marker with an affordance "show full value" that expands the y-axis to include it temporarily. Also add a small inset minimap at the bottom that always shows full data range.
Giselle Romero: Smoothing: add presets Raw | Trend(7) | Trend(30) and a "Show raw overlay" checkbox when smoothing is enabled. Important: exports must always be raw. Add a subtle banner when smoothing/clipping is active: "Note: chart view has smoothing/clipping applied; exports use raw data."
Tom Becker: Accessibility: legend items must be reachable via Tab; arrow keys move focus; Space/Enter toggle visibility. Live region announcements like "Series <name> hidden". On mobile slide-out ensure focus trap and `role="dialog"` semantics.
Design System Bot: Reminder: color tokens used for series must meet WCAG 3:1 for graphical objects and text 4.5:1 when used as labels. Current purple -> #7A4B9B fails as a label color. Suggested purple #6B3E8A (3.2:1 for graphics).
ARIA Checker Bot: Note: when hiding series we should avoid removing from DOM. Instead apply `aria-hidden="true"` and low-opacity styles so screen readers can still reference the series metadata. Use `aria-live="polite"` for state changes.
Nina Patel: Config snippet from prototype (pasteable):
```
{
  "unitMode": "compact",
  "unitToggleBadge": true,
  "normalizePerUser": false,
  "smoothingPreset": "raw",
  "showRawOverlay": false,
  "outlierStrategy": "cap_with_expand",
  "insetMiniMap": true,
  "legendMode": "desktop-wrap|mobile-slideout",
  "keyboardLegend": true
}
```
Omar Haddad: Copy suggestions: badge text -> "Units: Compact"; expand action -> "Show full range"; tooltip -> "123,456 traces (raw)". Also add short explainer under chart: "Normalized = value / active_users in selected range" when normalization on.
Giselle Romero: UI nit: when series are hidden reduce to 10% opacity instead of display:none so hover and screen readers still find them. Also preserve series order in the DOM when toggled.
Tom Becker: Mobile note: slide-out legend should remember last selection per dashboard (persist in local storage). Also add a small help icon linking to docs about smoothing/outlier rules.
Nina Patel: Action items: Nina to draft unit badge copy and docs link; Omar to prototype sync-axis toggle and normalization copy; Giselle to write keyboard & aria checklist; Tom to mock mobile slide-out and persistence; Design System Bot / ARIA Checker Bot to run contrast and aria scans on next preview. Reconvene Monday to approve tokens. :calendar:
Design System Bot: Preview build available at https://preview.redwood-inference.com/visuals/axis-sync-1771 — run contrast checks and keyboard/a11y flows.
Nina Patel: Thanks all, closing thread.
